In [[mathematics]], the '''Fontaine–Mazur conjectures''' are some conjectures introduced by {{harvs|txt|last1=Fontaine|author1-link=Jean-Marc Fontaine|last2=Mazur | author2-link=Barry Mazur|year=1995}} about when [[Galois module|''p''-adic representations]] of [[Galois group]]s of [[number field]]s can be constructed from representations on [[étale cohomology]] groups of varieties.<ref>{{cite book|author=Koch, Helmut|authorlink=Helmut Koch (mathematician)|chapter=Fontaine-Mazur Conjecture|title=Galois theory of p-extensions|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|year=2013|page=180|isbn=9783662049679|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nqfvCAAAQBAJ&pg=PA180}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author=Calegari, Frank|title=Even Galois representations and the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture|journal=Inventiones Mathematicae|year=2011|volume=185|issue=1|pages=1–16|url=http://www.math.uchicago.edu/~fcale/papers/EvenPotential.pdf|doi=10.1007/s00222-010-0297-0|arxiv=1012.4819|bibcode=2011InMat.185....1C|s2cid=8937648}} [https://arxiv.org/abs/0907.3427 arXiv preprint]</ref> Some cases of this conjecture in dimension 2 have been proved by {{harvtxt | Dieulefait | 2004}}.

The first conjecture stated by Fontaine and Mazur assumes that <math>\rho \colon \mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}|\mathbb{Q}) \to \mathrm{GL}_n(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_p)</math> is an irreducible representation that is unramified except at a finite number of primes and which is not the [[Tate twist]] of an even representation that factors through a finite quotient group of <math>\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}|\mathbb{Q})</math>.  It claims that in this case, <math>\rho</math> is associated to a cuspidal newform if and only if <math>\rho</math> is potentially semi-stable at <math>p</math>.
